text:
Earlier, Li Ru advised Dong Zhuo to promote famous scholars to gain public support. Dong Zhuo followed this advice in most cases and thus recommended the talented Cai Yong. Zhuo ordered his summons, but Cai Yong did not initially intend to go. Enraged, Zhuo sent a messenger to tell him: "If you do not come, I shall exterminate your entire clan." Fearing for his family, Cai Yong had no choice but to obey the command and arrived. Zhuo was delighted to see him and promoted him three times within a single month, appointing him as a Palace Attendant <note>original: "shizhong"</note>. He was treated with great favor and intimacy. <gloss>One who eternally relies on the powerful, like Yang Xiong following Wang Feng, will ultimately perish like a woodcutter on Mount Kunshan.</gloss>

Meanwhile, the Former Emperor <note>Young Emperor Ling of Han, Liu Bian</note>, Empress Dowager He, and Consort Tang were confined in the Palace of Eternal Peace. Their supplies of clothing and food gradually dwindled, and the Emperor’s tears never dried. <gloss>This mirrors the later King of Shu's lament about the days and months spent in such a place.</gloss> One day, happening to see a pair of swallows flying in the courtyard, the Emperor composed a poem. <gloss>In the empty courtyard, birds fly and dance; in the cold palace of an abandoned temple, his body remains isolated in his waning years.</gloss> The poem read:

The tender grass is green and thick with mist,
Lithely fly the pair of swallows.
A single ribbon of the Luo River flows green,
Upon the paths, the people are envied by me. <gloss>The first half describes the swallows and his distant gaze.</gloss>
Deep within the emerald clouds is the palace that was once my home. <gloss>Gazing toward the old palace, he cannot fly away; he is truly inferior to the pair of swallows that can return to their old nests. How tragic.</gloss>
Who will uphold loyalty and righteousness,
To vent the resentment within my heart? <gloss>The second half expresses his personal desire. The poetry is excellent.</gloss>

Dong Zhuo frequently sent people to spy on them. On that day, they obtained this poem and presented it to him. Zhuo said, "Using a poem of resentment as a pretext, I now have a justification to kill him." <gloss>To have a justification for the killing is a way to instruct the world.</gloss> He then ordered Li Ru to lead eighteen warriors into the palace to assassinate the Emperor. The Emperor was upstairs with the Empress Dowager and the Consort when a palace maid reported that Li Ru had arrived. The Emperor was greatly alarmed. Li Ru offered the Emperor poisoned wine. <gloss>The irony is that his poem invited this; drinking wine is considered the most elegant of matters.</gloss>

<summary>Dong Zhuo forces the scholar Cai Yong into service while the deposed Young Emperor languishes in captivity. After the Emperor writes a poem expressing his sorrow, Dong Zhuo uses it as an excuse to send Li Ru to execute him with poisoned wine.</summary>
<keywords>Dong Zhuo, Li Ru, Cai Yong, Young Emperor, Empress Dowager He, Consort Tang, assassination, poetry, poisoned wine</keywords>
